articles.title: Suitcase Murder Solved: Husband-Wife Duo Arrested for Killing Maid After Rape Threat in Hapur
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Hapur (Uttar Pradesh): Police have achieved a major breakthrough in the case of an unidentified woman’s decomposed body found inside a suitcase in a sugarcane field in the Pilkhuwa Kotwali area.

body.html:
Hapur (Uttar Pradesh): Police have achieved a major breakthrough in the case of an unidentified woman’s decomposed body found inside a suitcase in a sugarcane field in the Pilkhuwa Kotwali area. In a joint operation, the Pilkhuwa police and the district SWAT team arrested two accused — a husband and wife — on Sunday evening.

According to Additional Superintendent of Police Vineet Bhatnagar, the body was recovered on December 1, 2025, from a sugarcane field in the forest area of Chhijarsi village, near Rama Hospital on National Highway-9. Following the discovery, forensic experts, senior officers and local police teams reached the spot on the directions of the Superintendent of Police. Multiple teams were formed to identify the deceased and trace those involved.

Police arrested the accused near Duhri Cut. They were identified as Ankit, son of Amar Singh, a resident of Nawada Kalan under Simbhaoli police station in Hapur district, and his wife Kalista alias Kali, daughter of George Kerketta, a resident of Simdega district in Jharkhand. The deceased was identified as Sonia, a native of Jharkhand.

During interrogation, Ankit disclosed that he and his wife ran a firm named Srishti Enterprises and were involved in sending young women from poor and economically backward families in Jharkhand to Delhi-NCR as domestic helpers, allegedly collecting large sums of money in the process and often not paying the women.

Police said Sonia was brought from Jharkhand and was living with the accused. Ankit allegedly raped her and made an obscene video. When Sonia threatened to report the matter to the police, Ankit and his wife allegedly killed her on August 28, 2025, by beating her with kicks, punches and a stick.

To conceal the crime, the accused stuffed the body into a suitcase and dumped it in a sugarcane field in the Chhijarsi area. Police recovered the deceased’s mobile phone, three other mobile phones, two cash memo books and the stick used in the murder from the accused.

Investigators further revealed that another maid was present at the time of the murder and was allegedly threatened and forced to make a video confession near the body. Police said the accused later abandoned the suitcase near the Chhijarsi toll plaza on the Ghaziabad–Moradabad highway and fled.

ASP Vineet Bhatnagar said further legal proceedings are underway. The arresting team included Inspector-in-Charge Shyopal Singh along with officers from Pilkhuwa police station and the district SWAT team.

articles.title: Live-in Partner Beheaded Days Before Lover’s Wedding
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Yamunanagar (Haryana): The decapitated body of a young woman found in a poplar tree nursery in Bahadurpur village last Sunday has been identified as Uma, a resident of Saharanpur district in Uttar Pradesh.

body.html:
Yamunanagar (Haryana): The decapitated body of a young woman found in a poplar tree nursery in Bahadurpur village last Sunday has been identified as Uma, a resident of Saharanpur district in Uttar Pradesh. Police have arrested her lover, Bilal, for the murder, which was allegedly committed days before his scheduled wedding.

According to Yamunanagar police, the murder took place on December 6 near the Kalesar forest. The accused, Bilal, was to join his wedding procession on Sunday, but was arrested a day earlier following an investigation by the CIA-2 team. He was apprehended from Tidoli village in Saharanpur’s Nakur police station area and later sent on four-day police remand.

Police said Uma was previously married and the mother of a 10-year-old son. Due to disputes with her husband, she had been living separately for a long time. Her son lives with his father. Uma was residing alone in Gangotri Colony, Saharanpur, where Bilal frequently visited and reportedly bore most of her expenses.

Investigators revealed that Bilal and Uma had been in a live-in relationship for nearly two years. Meanwhile, Bilal’s family arranged his marriage elsewhere, scheduled for December 14. Uma allegedly opposed the marriage and was pressuring Bilal to marry her, which led to frequent disputes.

During interrogation, Bilal confessed that he planned Uma’s murder to escape the pressure. On December 6, he took her in his car on the pretext of a drive. Near Bahadurpur village, close to the Kalesar forest, he strangled her with the car seat belt. To conceal her identity, he slit her throat, removed her clothes, and dumped the body in a poplar nursery near the Paonta Highway. He later threw the severed head, wrapped in a polythene bag, into the Lal Dhang area of the Kalesar forest.

The naked, headless body was discovered on December 7, creating panic in the area. CCTV footage showing a car with a Saharanpur registration number, along with mobile location tracking and other technical evidence, led police to the accused. On Bilal’s disclosure, police recovered the severed head, clothes and a shawl. The murder weapon is yet to be recovered.

Superintendent of Police Kamaldeep Goyal said further investigation is underway, and the accused will be produced before the court after completion of remand proceedings. The deceased woman’s family, including her husband, has been informed.

articles.title: Overspeeding Car Mows Down Pedestrian in Telangana, Man Flung into Air — Shocking CCTV Emerges
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Medak (Telangana): A pedestrian was killed on the spot after being hit by an overspeeding car near Pothamsettipalle village in Kulcharam mandal while the vehicle was travelling from Medak towards Hyderabad.

body.html:
Medak (Telangana): A pedestrian was killed on the spot after being hit by an overspeeding car near Pothamsettipalle village in Kulcharam mandal while the vehicle was travelling from Medak towards Hyderabad.

The impact of the collision was so severe that the pedestrian was flung into the air and died instantly. Disturbing CCTV footage of the incident has surfaced, showing the reckless manner in which the car was being driven.

The deceased has been identified as Sridhar, a native of Karimnagar. After hitting him, the driver lost control of the car, which veered off the road and plunged into nearby agricultural fields.

Police have registered a case against the driver and initiated an investigation into the incident.

articles.title: White Owl Mistaken for ‘Garuda’, Villagers Begin Worship in Chhattisgarh — Video Sparks Debate
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bemetara (Chhattisgarh): A wave of religious fervour swept through Khamaria village in the Berla block after villagers began worshipping a white owl, believing it to be Garuda, the divine vehicle of Lord Vishnu.

body.html:
Bemetara (Chhattisgarh): A wave of religious fervour swept through Khamaria village in the Berla block after villagers began worshipping a white owl, believing it to be Garuda, the divine vehicle of Lord Vishnu.

The incident came to light when a rare, completely white bird was spotted on a farmer’s farm in the village. Mistaking the owl for Garuda, locals quickly gathered at the spot and started offering prayers. News of the bird’s appearance spread rapidly, drawing a large crowd to the farmhouse.

According to eyewitnesses, villagers sang hymns, performed rituals, and offered flowers and coconuts before the bird, treating it as a divine manifestation rather than a wild animal. A video of the incident has since surfaced, showing devotees worshipping the bird with deep faith.

However, the condition of the owl raised concerns, as it appeared visibly frightened by the crowd, loud chants and constant movement around it.

articles.title: Wedding Turns Into War: Dowry Demand, Bride Walks Out, Groom Alleges Hostage Drama in Bareilly
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bareilly (Uttar Pradesh): What was meant to be the happiest day of a couple’s life descended into chaos after the groom allegedly demanded a car and ₹20 lakh as dowry moments before the wedding vows, leading to police intervention and the marriage being called off.

body.html:
Bareilly (Uttar Pradesh): What was meant to be the happiest day of a couple’s life descended into chaos after the groom allegedly demanded a car and ₹20 lakh as dowry moments before the wedding vows, leading to police intervention and the marriage being called off.

According to reports, the groom demanded a Brezza car and ₹20 lakh in cash just before the wedding rituals, stating that he would not proceed with the marriage unless his demands were met. The sudden demand caused panic at the venue, following which the police were called.

Witnessing her family’s distress, the bride refused to go ahead with the marriage. Quoted by Dainik Bhaskar, she said she did not wish to marry “dowry-greedy people” and could not spend her life with someone who disrespected and humiliated her family in front of the guests.

Police detained the groom and his brother-in-law for questioning. However, no formal complaint was filed by the bride’s family.

The couple had got engaged in May, during which the bride’s family allegedly spent around ₹3 lakh. It is also claimed that the groom had already received a gold ring, a chain, and ₹5 lakh in cash. Additionally, the bride’s family reportedly gave an air conditioner, refrigerator, washing machine, household items, jewellery, and ₹1.20 lakh.

The wedding was scheduled for Friday. The wedding procession arrived and rituals were completed up to the stage of taking wedding vows, when the fresh dowry demand was allegedly made.

In a major twist, the groom, identified as Rishabh Saxena (29), has denied the allegations. He claimed that he was body-shamed by the bride’s family and later by the bride herself. He further alleged that his family members were held hostage on the wedding day, jewellery and valuables were looted, and that the bride’s family is now demanding ₹50 lakh after the wedding was cancelled.

Police said the matter is under verification and further action will be taken based on evidence.

articles.title: Bengaluru’s ‘Illicit Affairs Capital’ Tag Fuels Fresh Scandal: Housewife Elopes With Police Constabl
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A recent report claiming Bengaluru tops the country in illicit affairs has sparked debate, and a fresh case from Karnataka has added fuel to the controversy.

body.html:
A recent report claiming Bengaluru tops the country in illicit affairs has sparked debate, and a fresh case from Karnataka has added fuel to the controversy.

In a shocking incident, a housewife from Mysuru allegedly eloped with a police constable from North Karnataka, leaving behind her 12-year-old son. The woman, identified as Monica, reportedly ran away with Hoysala driver Raghavendra, attached to the HSR police station in Bengaluru.

According to sources, Monica had been married twice earlier. She separated from her first husband and later married her second, with whom she was living until recently. In June, Monica and Raghavendra reportedly came into contact through Instagram. The online interaction soon progressed to daily phone conversations, which allegedly developed into a romantic relationship.

Three months later, Monica lodged a complaint against her second husband at a police station, stating she wanted to improve her life and asked the police to call her husband for counselling. Acting on the complaint, Chandra Layout police summoned her husband to the station.

While her husband was on his way to the police station, Monica allegedly fled her home with 160 grams of gold ornaments and ₹1.80 lakh in cash. When questioned at the police station, her husband attempted to contact Monica, but she did not answer his calls. Suspecting foul play, he later filed a missing complaint at Chandra Layout police station.

During the investigation, it emerged that Monica had eloped with police constable Raghavendra. Following this revelation, senior police officials placed Raghavendra under suspension. Further investigation into the case is ongoing.

articles.title: Suspicion Turns Deadly: Gwalior Man Kills Wife Over Doubt, Arrested Within 24 Hours
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Gwalior: A man allegedly murdered his wife over suspicion of her character in Khatik Mohalla under the Indarganj police station area of Gwalior.

body.html:
Gwalior: A man allegedly murdered his wife over suspicion of her character in Khatik Mohalla under the Indarganj police station area of Gwalior. The accused, Dharmendra Maurya (48), attacked his wife, Renu Maurya (42), with a mogri (iron mace) late on Wednesday night (10 Dec 2025), killing her on the spot.

According to police, Dharmendra had long suspected his wife’s character after seeing her riding a bike with a young man. He repeatedly questioned her about the man’s identity, but Renu refused to disclose details, leading to frequent disputes between the couple.

On Wednesday night, the argument escalated. In a fit of rage and allegedly under the influence of alcohol, Dharmendra assaulted Renu with the weapon, inflicting fatal head injuries. At the time of the incident, their son and other family members, including the grandmother Kalavati and younger daughter Mansi, were present in the house. The child reportedly attempted to help his injured mother before she succumbed to her injuries.

After the murder, the accused fled the scene with the weapon. During interrogation, police said Dharmendra confessed to hiding the mogri near bushes after visiting the Achaleshwar temple. Based on his statement, the weapon was recovered.

Police registered a murder case, sent the body for post-mortem, seized evidence from the spot, and called in the FSL team for investigation. Due to swift action, the accused was arrested within 24 hours and has been sent to jail.

Family members told police that the couple had been married for 25 years. Renu, who had three children from a previous marriage, worked at a private school due to financial difficulties, which often led to quarrels, as her husband reportedly opposed her job.

The incident has shocked the locality and created panic and outrage among residents. Police said further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Speeding Cop’s Thar Turns Killer on Highway: One Dead, SI Suspended
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A female sub-inspector of the Madhya Pradesh Police allegedly ran over four people with her speeding Thar SUV on the Indore–Bhopal highway late on Friday evening(12 Dec 2025) , leaving one person dead and three others injured.

body.html:
A female sub-inspector of the Madhya Pradesh Police allegedly ran over four people with her speeding Thar SUV on the Indore–Bhopal highway late on Friday evening(12 Dec 2025) , leaving one person dead and three others injured.

According to police, the accident occurred when a red Thar vehicle (registration number MP04 ZW 7803) lost control, mounted the pavement and rammed into roadside blanket shops, also hitting a motorcycle. At the time of the incident, two victims were sitting inside a blanket shop, while the other two were riding the bike.

All four injured were rushed to Bhopal for treatment, where two were reported to be in critical condition. Vijay, one of the bike riders, later succumbed to his injuries during treatment at Narmada Trauma Hospital.

The deceased and injured have been identified as:
1. Vakil (28), son of Girdhari, resident of Ujjain
2. Lakhan (16), son of Madan Lal, resident of Mahidpur, Ujjain
3. Hridesh Rajoria (40), son of Rajaram Rajoria, resident of Ratibad, Bhopal
4. Vijay, son of Rajaram, resident of Ratibad, Bhopal

Hridesh and Vijay were brothers.

The Thar was being driven by Kiran Singh Rajput, a female sub-inspector posted at Ashta police station in Madhya Pradesh.

Kotwali Police Station in-charge Ravindra Yadav said a case has been registered against the driver and an investigation has been initiated. The preliminary probe has been handed over to the City Superintendent of Police (CSP), Sehore.

Eyewitnesses alleged that the vehicle was moving at very high speed, causing victims to be thrown off the road. Blanket seller Toofan Singh Banjara lodged the complaint at Kotwali Police Station.

CSP Dr Abhinandana Sharma confirmed that an FIR has been registered against SI Kiran Singh Rajput on the basis of the complaint. Treating the incident as serious negligence and misconduct, Sehore Superintendent of Police Deepak Kumar Shukla has suspended SI Kiran Singh Rajput and attached her to the Sehore Protection Centre.
